steps.name: QC and exploratory diagnostics on raw counts
steps.question: Are the 3 treated and 3 control liver samples free of outliers, batch structure, or mislabeling that would confound a treated-vs-control comparison, based on library size, PCA, and sample-sample correlation of the 12000 x 6 count matrix?
acceptance_criteria: Library size (total counts) reported per sample from counts.csv
PCA and hierarchical clustering / sample correlation heatmap computed on variance-stabilized or log-CPM counts, colored by condition from metadata.csv
Any sample flagged as an outlier or mis-clustering with its group is explicitly called out with the metric that flagged it
Gene count matrix confirmed to have genes as rows (or columns) matching the 6 sample IDs in metadata.csv, condition column identified

steps.name: Differential expression: treated vs control
steps.question: Which of the 12000 genes are differentially expressed between the 3 treated and 3 control liver samples (DESeq2 Wald test, BH-adjusted FDR < 0.05, with a log2FC threshold reported alongside)?
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 run with design ~condition on raw integer counts from counts.csv, condition levels set so treated is compared against control as reference
Output table includes gene symbol, baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj for all tested genes
Independent filtering applied and number of genes filtered out reported
Shrunken log2FC (apeglm or ashr) reported alongside raw MLE estimates given the small per-group n
Summary counts of significant genes at padj<0.05 and at padj<0.1 both reported, with the effect-size distribution of hits described
MA plot and volcano plot produced

steps.name: Power and precision assessment for the n=3 vs n=3 design
steps.question: Given 3 replicates per group, what is the statistical power/precision of the treated-vs-control DE call — how does gene-wise dispersion shrinkage behave, what minimum detectable fold-change is achievable at this sample size and the observed dispersion, and how stable are the significant gene calls to leave-one-out resampling?
acceptance_criteria: Gene-wise dispersion estimates vs DESeq2 fitted trend and shrinkage reported (dispersion plot), with commentary on how much shrinkage is needed at n=3 and the risk of residual dispersion misestimation

A power curve or simulation-based estimate (e.g. via a negative-binomial power calculation appropriate for n=3 vs n=3, using observed mean-dispersion relationship) reporting minimum detectable log2FC at 80% power for typical baseMean strata
Leave-one-out (drop one sample per group in turn) stability check on the top significant genes from T2S1, reporting what fraction of top hits are recovered across leave-one-out refits
A plain-language confidence statement: at n=3 per group, which effect sizes are reliably detectable versus which are underpowered, grounded in the numbers computed above, not asserted

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of DE genes
steps.question: Which WikiPathways human pathways are enriched among the genes significantly differentially expressed (padj<0.05) between treated and control liver samples identified in T2S1?
acceptance_criteria: Uses the human WikiPathways GMT reference confirmed present in the environment; if absent at run time, the step reports the gap and skips rather than fabricating results
Over-representation or GSEA-style enrichment run on the DESeq2 gene list from T2S1 (ranked by shrunken log2FC or stat for GSEA; padj<0.05 set for ORA)
Enrichment results reported with adjusted p-values (BH) and the member genes driving each significant pathway
Result explicitly flags that with n=3 per group, the input gene list itself carries the precision/power caveats from T3S1, so enrichment should be read as hypothesis-generating

plan.title: Liver DE: treated vs control (n=3/group) with power caveat
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq salmon gene counts (12000 genes x 6 samples used for analysis, 1 metadata column beyond sample id) for human liver, drug treatment vs control, 3 vs 3, unpaired, single batch. This is a minimal-replicate design: DESeq2/edgeR can still fit a negative-binomial model with 3 vs 3, but power to detect moderate fold-changes is limited and dispersion estimates are noisy, so the plan (1) runs a standard DESeq2 pipeline with QC (library size, PCA, sample correlation) to catch outliers/mislabeling before trusting any DE call, (2) performs the DE test with independent filtering and BH-FDR, (3) explicitly quantifies achieved power/precision for this n=3 design (e.g. dispersion shrinkage diagnostics, standard errors and effect-size confidence intervals per gene, and a power curve/simulation) so the confidence statement is quantitative rather than a hand-wave, and (4) runs pathway enrichment on the DE gene list against human WikiPathways gene sets to give biological context to whatever signal survives the small-n correction. Steps are ordered QC -> DE -> power/precision assessment -> enrichment, each depending on the prior step's output.
